item.title: On $c$-Normal Maximal Chains of Sylow Subgroups in Finite Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.26968v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be finite group. A subgroup $H$ of $G$ is said to be $c$-normal in $G$ if there exists a normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ such that $G = HN$ and $H\cap N\leq H_G$, where $H_G$ is the core of $H$ in $G$. Let $P$ be a nontrivial $p$-group. A chain of subgroups $1=P_0 <P_1<\cdots P_{n-1}<P_n=P$ is called a maximal chain of $P$ provided that $|P_i:P_{i-1}|=p$ for $i=1,2,\ldots n-1$. In this paper, we determine the structure of finite groups having $c$-normal subgroups of of a maximal chain of Sylow subgroups. We obtain new characterizations of finite $p$-nilpotent and supersolvable groups.
item.dc:creator: Wei Meng, Feiyu Geng

item.title: Quantum polynomial-time conjugacy in metabelian groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.27250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the conjugacy problem in finitely presented metabelian groups with a fixed number of generators is solvable in bounded-error quantum polynomial time, uniformly in the defining relations of the group. Both the group presentation and the words representing the elements are part of the input. The main ingredient is a quantum polynomial-time algorithm for computing all multiplicative relations among a fixed number of units in a commutative affine $\mathbb Z$-algebra presented with a fixed number of variables. The algorithm reduces the problem to computations in finite-dimensional algebras over $\mathbb Q$ and finite rings by identifying the lattice of exponent vectors whose corresponding products are algebraic over the coefficient field. An effective arithmetic splitting combines the rational and finite-ring computations. The proof uses effective bounds for polynomial equations, algorithms for finite-dimensional commutative algebras, quantum integer factorization, and finite abelian hidden-subgroup algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Alexei Miasnikov, Alexander Ushakov

item.title: Ordered frequency in relatively hyperbolic groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.27268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study word frequencies along infinite strings whose finite prefixes lie in a regular language of geodesic representatives of group elements. Let \((G,\mathcal H)\) be a non-elementary relatively hyperbolic pair, and suppose that, over a finite symmetric generating set, there is a prefix-closed regular language containing exactly one shortest word representing each element of \(G\). Modeling this language using a finite-state Markov chain, we define a probability measure on the space of infinite strings whose finite prefixes are words belonging to this language. Each such string labels a geodesic ray emanating from the identity. We show there is a continuous surjection from this space onto the Bowditch boundary, and the pushforward of the probability measure under this map is a Patterson--Sullivan probability obtained as a weak limit of weighted counts of group elements. For a word \(w\), the ordered frequency of \(w\) along a given labeled ray is the limiting proportion of consecutive nonoverlapping tuples of length \(|w|\) that exactly spell \(w\). For almost every infinite string under the constructed measure, these frequencies exist simultaneously for all nonempty geodesic words, with no restriction on their lengths. Consequently, almost every boundary point with respect to this Patterson--Sullivan probability is the endpoint of at least one such ray along which all these frequencies exist. In particular, after possibly enlarging the generating set, these results apply when the peripheral subgroups are virtually abelian.
item.dc:creator: Dominic Bair

item.title: Linear $2$-Group Actions With Exactly One Regular Orbit
item.description: arXiv:2610.27536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite $2$-group and $V$ a finite faithful irreducible $G$-module. We show that if $G$ has exactly one regular orbit on $V$, then the characteristic $q$ of $V$ is a Fermat prime, $V$ is irreducible over ${\Bbb F}_q$, ${\rm dim}_{{\Bbb F}_q}V$ is a power of $2$, and the centraliser of $G$ in ${\rm GL}(V)$ embeds into $G$. For every Fermat prime $q$ and every $m\ge 1$ we determine the largest orbit size $2^{x_m}$ of a Sylow $2$-subgroup $P_m$ of ${\rm GL}_{2^{m-1}}(q)$ on its natural module $V_m$, and the number of orbits of this size, which is $1$, $2$, or $3$. Our main result is that for every Fermat prime $q$ and every $m\ge 1$ there is an irreducible subgroup of $P_m$ of order $2^{x_m}$ that has exactly one regular orbit on $V_m$. In this respect $p=2$ behaves like $p=3$, and unlike the Mersenne primes $p\ge 7$ studied in an earlier paper. The proof places a group related to a Singer cycle into every block of $q-1$ coordinates. This reduces the problem, for all Fermat primes at once, to a question about subgroups of a Sylow $2$-subgroup of a symmetric group acting on subsets, which we answer by means of fibre products. We also determine which largest orbits occur in two small levels, and we classify the examples in some small cases with the help of a computer.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Michael Keller, Jeffrey M. Riedl

item.title: Maximal ranks of free abelian subgroups of generalized cactus groups associated with finite Coxeter systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.27716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the maximum ranks of free abelian subgroups of generalized cactus groups associated with finite Coxeter systems. To obtain the upper bounds, we use the cubical flat torus theorem of Wise and Woodhouse. We then verify the sharpness of these upper bounds by constructing free abelian subgroups of the corresponding ranks. Our result shows that the maximal ranks of free abelian subgroups of ordinary cactus groups can be larger than conjectured by Genevois. As an application, we show that these groups are not quasi-isometric to any right-angled Artin group unless they are virtually free abelian.
item.dc:creator: Jan Kim, Junseok Kim

item.title: Classification of finite subgroups of generalized cactus groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.27721v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify the finite groups that embed into generalized cactus groups $C_W$ associated with arbitrary Coxeter systems $(W,S)$. Every finite subgroup is conjugate to a subgroup of $C_{W_T}$ for some spherical subset $T\subseteq S$. This reduces the classification to explicit lists of finite groups for the finite irreducible Coxeter systems. For types $B$, $D$, $E$, $F$, and $H$, we analyze cube stabilizers to obtain these lists. For type $I_2(p)$, we determine $C_{W(I_2(p))}$ directly from its defining presentation. We explicitly realize every listed group as a subgroup of the corresponding generalized cactus group. When $S$ is finite, we determine the largest order and all possible orders of finite subgroups of $C_W$. In type $A$, we prove directly that a finite group embeds into the ordinary cactus group $J_n$ if and only if it embeds into a Sylow $2$-subgroup of the symmetric group $S_n$. We also give weighted embedding criteria in types $A$ and $B$ and counterexamples to Genevois's conjecture on finite subgroups of cactus groups.
item.dc:creator: Junseok Kim

item.title: Finite groups with large sum of element orders compared to cyclic groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.27846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a finite group $G$ let $\psi(G)$ denote the sum of the orders of elements in $G$. If $G$ has order $n$ then, by a result of Amiri, Jafarian Amiri and Isaacs, $\psi(G)\le\psi(C_n)$, where $C_n$ is the cyclic group of order $n$. We determine all finite groups such that $\psi(G)\ge\frac{1}{3}\psi(C_n)$.
item.dc:creator: P\'eter P. P\'alfy, Alex D. Simonyi

item.title: Thompson's group $F$ is not weakly amenable
item.description: arXiv:2610.27932v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F$ be Thompson's group, and let $D$ be the set of dyadic rationals in $[0,1]$. We give an embedding of $\mathbb Z^{(D)}\rtimes F$ into $F$, where the semidirect product is defined by the natural action of $F$ on $D$. Using this embedding, we deduce from the nonamenability of $F$ that $F$ is not weakly amenable.
item.dc:creator: Koji Fujiwara

item.title: Wielandt subgroups of nilpotent residuals and Fitting-height bounds
item.description: arXiv:2610.28082v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a finite group $G$, let $\mathrm W(G)$ be the intersection of the normalizers of the nilpotent residuals of the subnormal subgroups of $G$, and let $\ell_{\mathrm W}(G)$ be the length of the associated upper series. Thus $\mathrm W(G)=G$ exactly when all these residuals are normal in $G$. We prove that every finite soluble group satisfies $\ell_{\mathrm W}(G)\le h(G)\le4\ell_{\mathrm W}(G)$, where $h(G)$ is the Fitting height, and that $h(G)\le3\ell_{\mathrm W}(G)$ if $|G|$ is odd or the Sylow $2$-subgroups of $G$ are abelian. Both constants are attained at every length, the constant $4$ by $\{2,3\}$-groups. Moreover, every pair $(n,h)$ with $n\le h\le4n$ occurs as $(\ell_{\mathrm W}(G),h(G))$. The constant $4$ comes from primitive groups. A soluble primitive group $V\rtimes M$ satisfies $\mathrm W(V\rtimes M)=V\rtimes M$ if and only if every abelian subgroup of $\mathrm F(M)$ is cyclic. It then has Fitting height four if and only if $\mathrm F(M)=C\times Q_8$, with $C$ cyclic, and $M$ induces the full group $\mathrm{Out}(Q_8)\cong S_3$. We also determine when the base group of a soluble regular wreath product is the first term of the series.
item.dc:creator: L\"u Gong, Yan Yan, Enric Cosme Ll\'opez

item.title: Determinant characters and multiplicative solubility of finite skew braces
item.description: arXiv:2610.28420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $B$ be a finite skew brace. We prove that if the additive derived subgroup $(B,+)'$ is nilpotent, then the multiplicative group $(B,\cdot)$ is soluble. In particular, this holds for finite skew braces with supersoluble or metabelian additive group.
item.dc:creator: Marco Damele

item.title: Galois Groups of Shifted Exponential Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.26873v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a fixed integer $a>0$, consider the shifted truncations \[ F_{n,a}(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}\frac{x^j}{(a+j)!} \] and their monic integral normalizations $P_{n,a}(x)=(n+a)!F_{n,a}(x)$. In this paper, we prove that, for every fixed integer $a>0$, the set of $n$ for which $F_{n,a}$ is irreducible has natural density one. We also prove that $G_{n,a}:=\text{Gal}(F_{n,a}/\mathbb{Q})$ is primitive for all sufficiently large $n$ for which $F_{n,a}$ is irreducible, and that it contains $A_n$ for a density-one set of $n$. Finally, we prove that, for any fixed integer $a>0$, the discriminant of $F_{n,a}$ is a nonsquare for a density-one set of $n$, and hence that $\text{Gal}(F_{n,a}/\mathbb{Q})=S_n$ for a density-one set of $n$. To obtain irreducibility with density one, we use a result of Shorey and Tijdeman, as well as a smooth-number density argument. Following that, two explicitly chosen Newton polygons give cycles that force primitivity, and hence containment of $A_n$. Finally, an exact computation of the valuation of the discriminant at primes satisfying $\frac n2+a<p<n+a$ implies that the discriminant is a nonsquare for odd $a$ and almost all $n$, implying the group is $S_n$ in those cases. For even $a$, we contradict the existence of many square discriminants by showing they generate a family of biased Dirichlet characters. These imply many zeros off of the critical line, which contradict standard zero-density bounds.
item.dc:creator: Shachar Weinbaum

item.title: Median spaces with the strict separation property and superrigidity of actions
item.description: arXiv:2610.27866v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce strictly separated median spaces, prove structural results and establish superrigidity for actions of higher rank lattices on the latter. We consider two different approach, the first one relies on the construction of a boundary map and the second one is self-contained and relies on the median geometry of the space of sections taking values in a median space.
item.dc:creator: Indira Chatterji, Lamine Messaci

item.title: Elements of the Green ring related to Alperin's weight conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.27988v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: J. L. Alperin introduced his celebrated weight conjecture, a major question in the modular representation theory of finite groups, which has now been studied for several decades. Alperin viewed this conjecture as the beginning of a ``Lie theory for the general finite group", as the title of the article indicates. This paper is intended as a tribute to Alperin's insight. In this note, we place an emphasis on projective modules and putting the numerical questions arising from the weight conjecture into a ``module form" within the appropriate Green ring of RG, when G is a finite group, and R is a suitable complete discrete valuation ring with residue field of prime characteristic p. We believe that this work moves in the direction of a structural approach to Alperin's weight conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Geoffrey R. Robinson

item.title: Random $C^*$-subalgebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.28295v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a discrete countable group $\Gamma$, we introduce the concept of random subalgebras of the reduced group $C^*$-algebra $C_r^*(\Gamma)$. This extends the existing theory of invariant random subgroups and the one of invariant random subalgebras of the group von Neumann algebra ${\rm L}(\Gamma)$. As applications, we provide a characterisation of $C^*$-simplicity, a condition for amenability of the group and show the existence and uniqueness of a maximal nuclear $\Gamma$-invariant unital $C^*$-subalgebra of $C^*_r(\Gamma)$. Moreover, we give a topological characterisation of exactness of any separable unital $C^*$-algebra. Finally, we study exotic random subalgebras of $C^*_r(\Gamma)$ and super-exotic random subalgebras of ${\rm L}(\Gamma)$, that is, random subalgebras which do not arise purely from random subgroups of $\Gamma$ and not from random subalgebras of $C^*_r(\Gamma)$, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Fima, Hanna Oppelmayer, Leyan Tao

item.title: C*-selflessness and $\mathcal{Z}$-stability for Thompson's group $F$
item.description: arXiv:2610.28473v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the reduced C*-algebra of Thompson's group $F$ is $\mathcal{Z}$-stable and selfless.
item.dc:creator: Chris Bruce, Shirly Geffen

item.title: Twisted Post-Groups and Skew Trusses
item.description: arXiv:2307.10535v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: To understand the origin of post-groups introduced by Bai, Guo, Sheng, and Tang from the perspective of rings, we introduce the notion of (weak) twisted post-groups. First, we show that every element of a twisted post-group belongs to a unique group, and that a twisted post-group can be viewed as the disjoint union of such groups. Next, we prove that the category of weak twisted post-groups is isomorphic to the category of skew trusses, and that every two-sided twisted post-group admits the structure of a two-sided skew brace. It follows that every abelian two-sided twisted post-group gives rise to a radical ring. We then introduce twisted post-Lie algebras and investigate their algebraic properties, showing that differentiating a twisted post-Lie group yields a twisted post-Lie algebra. Finally, we consider the linearization of (weak) twisted post-groups and propose the notion of (weak) twisted post-Hopf algebras. We show that every twisted post-Hopf algebra gives rise to another Hopf algebra, called the sub-adjacent Hopf algebra.
item.dc:creator: Shukun Wang

item.title: Geometries for Groups
item.description: arXiv:2511.03887v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a "continuous converse" to the Milnor-Schwarz lemma. Given any topological group $G$ and any left-invariant, large scale geodesic pseudometric $d$ giving an identity neighborhood finite diameter (for example, the word metric with respect to an open generating set), we construct a geodesic metric space $X$ equipped with a continuous, isometric, cobounded action of $G$ such that $(G,d)$ and $X$ are quasi-isometric via any orbit map.
item.dc:creator: Robert Alonzo Lyman

item.title: On algebraic and arithmetic properties of monoids of product-$K$ sequences
item.description: arXiv:2607.03020v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be a group and $K$ be a normal subgroup of $G$. A sequence over $G$ is a finite collection of terms from $G$, where repetition is allowed, and the order is disregarded. A product-$K$ sequence is a sequence whose terms can be ordered such that their product in $G$ belongs to $K$. The set $\mathcal B_K (G)$ of all product-$K$ sequences over $G$ forms a monoid, called the monoid of product-$K$ sequences, under the operation of sequence concatenation. In this paper, we investigate the algebraic and arithmetic properties of the monoid $\mathcal B_K (G)$. Among our main results, we provide precise characterizations of when $\mathcal B_K (G)$ satisfies key properties, namely being (transfer) Krull, a (seminormal) C-monoid, or (half-)factorial. After that, we study the Isomorphism Problem for monoids of product-$K$ sequences. Our results generalize existing frameworks, making them applicable to both the classical abelian and the more recently developed non-abelian settings.
item.dc:creator: Jun Seok Oh, Doniyor Yazdonov

item.title: An infinite family of counterexamples to the Polycirculant Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2607.23423v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We disprove the Polycirculant Conjecture, which states that every transitive 2-closed permutation group is non-elusive, i.e. contains a derangement of prime order. In fact, we prove a stronger result, answering a long-standing question of Maru\v{s}i\v{c} and Jordan: there exists a vertex-transitive graph admitting no semiregular automorphism. To do so, we employ recently developed methods of Chen et al. for constructing elusive groups via non-split extensions, allowing us to construct an elusive group $7^6.\mathrm{PSU}_3(3)$ of degree 16,464. We show that this group is the full automorphism group of seven of its orbital graphs and hence is 2-closed. Our example extends to infinitely many counterexamples of the Polycirculant Conjecture, and infinitely many vertex-transitive graphs admitting no semiregular automorphism.
item.dc:creator: Saul D. Freedman, Melissa Lee

item.title: Near full groups of bounded type, II
item.description: arXiv:2607.26572v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study when a finitely generated group of bounded type contains the AF alternating group of the tail groupoid of its defining Bratteli diagram. This containment is an input to the full group completion theorem of Part I. We give sufficient conditions for this containment, in which selectors separate inherited diagonal actions, and an exact criterion for finite regular coverings. In the covering case, the intersection with the AF alternating group is the centralizer of the deck transformations commuting with the adjoined AF permutations. The formula classifies all subgroups between the canonical lift of the base AF alternating group and the AF alternating group of the covering. In particular, the lift is maximal exactly when the deck group has prime order, and cyclic coverings yield finitely generated groups whose intersections with the AF alternating group of the covering realize these subgroups. We identify fragmentations that produce the required selectors. For periodic fragmentations of the directed generator in the modified Fabrykowski--Gupta group, surjectivity of the activity subspace onto each pair of consecutive coordinates gives containment with absorption delay at most two. A five-periodic example also satisfies this condition, although its activity subspace has dual distance two. The original four-periodic fragmentation group has index four in its topological full group.
item.dc:creator: Zheng Kuang

item.title: Dimension formula for harmonic measures in invariant random graphs on Gromov hyperbolic spaces
item.description: arXiv:2403.11406v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For random walks in various group-invariant random graphs on Gromov hyperbolic spaces, we show that the associated harmonic measures are exact dimensional and their Hausdorff dimensions are equal to the entropy over the speed, Our method is inspired by cluster relations introduced by Gaboriau and applies to percolation clusters on hyperbolic groups and Poisson--Voronoi tessellations on rank one Riemannian symmetric spaces.
item.dc:creator: Kohki Sakamoto

item.title: Integral quasi-strongly regular Cayley graphs
item.description: arXiv:2511.14496v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quasi-strongly regular graphs form a significant generalization of strongly regular graphs. We study the eigenvalues of a family of such graphs, $\Gamma_H(G)$, constructed from a finite group $G$ and a subgroup $H$. Our main results include a sufficient condition for $\Gamma_H(G)$ to be integral and an explicit computation of its entire spectrum when $H$ is normal, revealing that the spectrum in this case depends only on $|G|$ and the index $[G:H]$.
item.dc:creator: Sauvik Poddar, Sucharita Biswas, Angsuman Das

item.title: Affine diagram categories, algebras and monoids
item.description: arXiv:2512.05510v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce and study several affine (=annular in this paper) versions of the classical diagram algebras such as Temperley-Lieb, partition, Brauer, Motzkin, rook Brauer, rook, planar partition, and planar rook algebras. We give generators and relation presentation for them and their associated categories, study their representation theory, and the asymptotic behavior of tensor products of their representations in the monoid case. Under a mild hypothesis, we also prove a previous conjecture concerning the asymptotic growth of the number of indecomposable summands in the tensor powers of representations for finite monoids.
item.dc:creator: David He, Daniel Tubbenhauer
